name.text: Q7 - Discovering the hidden trial in farmer IDs

questiontext.text:
Rescuing a hidden variable: two cassava trials

In the Nigeria example in the chapter, the frequencies of option_a initially seem unbalanced. Looking more closely at the id column reveals that the data come from two trials: Osun and Benue.

Here is a smaller illustrative dataset with three farmers and three varieties. Each farmer has one preferred variety recorded in option_a.

Example IDoption_a
Osun-{@idstart@}Variety A
Osun-{@idstart+1@}Variety B
Benue-{@idstart+2@}Variety C

In the full illustrative dataset, the frequencies are:

TrialVariety AVariety BVariety CTotal
Osun{@osun_each@}{@osun_each@}{@osun_each@}{@osun_total@}
Benue{@benue_a@}{@benue_b@}{@benue_c@}{@benue_total@}
All records{@pooled_a@}{@pooled_b@}{@pooled_c@}{@grand_total@}

A. Predict

Why might the pooled option_a frequencies be misleading? [[input:predict]] [[validation:predict]] [[feedback:prtpredict]]

B. Rescue the hidden variable

Which part of the ID identifies the trial? [[input:idpart]] [[validation:idpart]] [[feedback:prtidpart]]

What kind of column would be suitable for a new trial variable in R-Instat? [[input:trialtype]] [[validation:trialtype]] [[feedback:prttrialtype]]

C. Investigate the frequencies

How many farmers are in the Osun trial? [[input:osuncount]] [[validation:osuncount]] [[feedback:prtosuncount]]

How many farmers chose Variety C in the Benue trial? [[input:benueccount]] [[validation:benueccount]] [[feedback:prtbenueccount]]

If you make a frequency table of option_awithout filtering by trial, how many farmers chose Variety A? [[input:pooledacount]] [[validation:pooledacount]] [[feedback:prtpooledacount]]

[[hint title="Hint: pooled frequencies"]]

A pooled frequency is the sum of the frequencies for that variety in Osun and Benue.

[[/hint]]

D. Interpret

After filtering the data to Osun only, which statement is true? [[input:osuninterpret]] [[validation:osuninterpret]] [[feedback:prtosuninterpret]]

Which is the most appropriate next step if you want to investigate whether the variety choices differ between the two trials? [[input:nextstep]] [[validation:nextstep]] [[feedback:prtnextstep]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

The ID contains the trial name before the hyphen. Splitting the ID on the hyphen allows us to create a trial column. Since the values Osun and Benue are categories, a factor is suitable for this column.

In this illustrative dataset, Osun has {@osun_each@} observations for each of the three varieties, giving \(3\times {@osun_each@}={@osun_total@}\) farmers in total.

Benue has {@benue_a@}, {@benue_b@} and {@benue_c@} observations for Varieties A, B and C respectively. In particular, Variety C has {@benue_c@} observations in Benue.

Pooling both trials gives \({@osun_each@}+{@benue_a@}={@pooled_a@}\) observations for Variety A.

The pooled frequencies differ because the two trials have different frequency patterns. Filtering to Osun reveals equal frequencies for the three varieties. For an investigation of the two trials, create the trial factor and compare separate frequency tables or a table grouped by trial.

In the chapter's larger Nigeria dataset, splitting the ID reveals Osun and Benue. Filtering to Osun gives 300 observations across eight cassava varieties, with 37 or 38 farmers per variety. The smaller numbers above are for practice, not the chapter's actual data.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Read the Variety C entry in the Benue row.

falsefeedback.text: Use the Benue row, not the pooled row, for Variety C.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Splitting on the hyphen recovers the trial name.

falsefeedback.text: The text Osun or Benue appears before the hyphen.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Separate or grouped tables retain the trial information.

falsefeedback.text: To investigate differences between trials, keep the trial variable in the analysis.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Add the three Osun frequencies.

falsefeedback.text: The Osun total is three times the frequency of each variety in Osun.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Osun is balanced across the three illustrative varieties.

falsefeedback.text: Check the Osun row: the three variety counts are identical.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Add the Variety A counts from both trials.

falsefeedback.text: Add Variety A in Osun and Variety A in Benue.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Pooling can hide important differences between trials.

falsefeedback.text: Look at the Osun and Benue rows before interpreting the pooled totals.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Osun and Benue are categories with no inherent order.

falsefeedback.text: A factor is appropriate for a fixed set of unordered trial names.
